name: Novafold Pharmaceuticals GraftSkin TS-7 Bioprinted Dermal Replacement Sheet
product_name: Novafold Pharmaceuticals GraftSkin TS-7 Bioprinted Dermal Replacement Sheet
description:
The GraftSkin TS-7 is a roll-format bioprinted dermal replacement product manufactured in standardized 20cm x 40cm sheets, each seeded with the patient's own keratinocytes and fibroblasts cultured from a small biopsy sample processed on-site using Novafold's proprietary rapid-culture bioreactor cartridge. Unlike earlier graft technologies that required weeks of laboratory preparation, the TS-7 system produces a viable, patient-matched dermal sheet in approximately 72 hours, dramatically reducing the rejection risk that plagued allograft procedures. The sheet itself is a tri-layer construct: an outer silicone temporary barrier, a mid-layer of cultured epidermis, and a dermal analog matrix seeded with vascular precursor cells that integrate with host tissue to restore blood supply within 10-14 days.

The TS-7 system is designed to treat large-area burns, traumatic degloving injuries, and — increasingly commonly in GLMZ — the surgical removal of unwanted subdermal implants or corporate identification tattoos. The rapid-culture bioreactor cartridge slots into a compact benchtop unit the size of a microwave oven, making the system deployable in field hospitals, corporate medical bays, and — with the grey-market cartridge adapters sold by unlicensed vendors — in back-alley clinics. Novafold maintains strict cartridge serialization to prevent off-label deployment, but counterfeit cartridges using generic culture media have proliferated throughout the Undersprawl.

Applications have expanded well beyond trauma medicine. Cosmetic modification clinics use TS-7 sheets to provide seamless coverage following subdermal implant revision, and identity-change fixers prize the system for its ability to alter fingerprint patterns and remove biometric skin markers. The corporate security community is acutely aware of this second use case, and Novafold faces ongoing legal pressure from Tessera Corponation and Arcturus Defense Solutions to add biometric watermarks to all cultured sheets — a proposal Novafold has publicly resisted while quietly lobbying against its implementation.

social_impact: The GraftSkin TS-7 has quietly become one of the most politically charged medical technologies in GLMZ, sitting at the intersection of bodily autonomy and corporate surveillance. For trauma patients in Tier 2 hospitals, it represents a genuine leap in burn care outcomes. For Tier 5 residents trying to shed corporate citizenship markers, escape indentured contracts, or simply change their identities, it is a tool of liberation — and for the corporations whose biometric infrastructure depends on skin-based identification, it is an existential threat. The ongoing debate over mandatory watermarking has spilled into public discourse, with civil liberties advocates and corporate security lobbies staging increasingly heated public confrontations.
story_hooks: A key witness in a corporate espionage trial has had their fingerprints replaced using a TS-7 sheet — the players must find another way to prove identity before the case collapses
Novafold's rapid-culture bioreactor facility is targeted by a Tessera Corponation black ops team seeking to steal the watermarking-resistance formula before a regulatory vote
A batch of counterfeit TS-7 cartridges is producing sheets contaminated with a slow-activating dermal neurotoxin — someone is using the grey market supply chain as a delivery mechanism

A Tier 5 underground railroad is using GraftSkin TS-7 to help indentured workers shed their corporate biometric markers and escape — the players must decide whether to expose, protect, or join the operation
